evidence: Caes. BC 3.92.1: tantum erat relictum spatiī
Lucr. 1.426: locus ac spatium, quod ināne vocāmus
terms.comment: The room or extent a thing has, or the distance between things; also a space of time (see period).

terms.gloss: room, a place for someone or something
evidence: Plaut. Poen. 23: līberīs ut sit locus
terms.comment: Room for someone: est locus, there is room; locum ad spectandum dare, to give someone a place to watch from (Cic. Mur. 73, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a gap, the space between two things

phrases.latin: Inter duās aciēs tantum erat relictum spatiī, ut satis esset ad concursum utriusque exercitūs.
phrases.english: Between the two lines enough space had been left for each army to charge.

phrases.latin: servī nē obsideant, līberīs ut sit locus
phrases.english: slaves must not take up the seats, so that there is room for free men

sources: Lewis & Short: spatium · Lewis & Short: locus · Lewis & Short: intervallum
